source.title: Identifying Functionally Important Features with End-to-End Sparse Dictionary Learning

record.file_problem: This is an Alignment Forum summary of the paper with comments, not the paper's full text.
record.tranche_reason: The study compares a standard SAE objective with end-to-end objectives and reports a geometric proxy for feature splitting, finding less clustering in the end-to-end variants. This refines the claim that splitting depends on the SAE objective, but does not directly establish that splitting is an artifact or that features fail to reflect model units.
record.gate_note: The study measures nearest-neighbor cosine similarity within SAE dictionaries and interprets tighter clustering as a proxy for more splitting. Its performance and downstream reconstruction results do not measure splitting. The introduction's description of prior feature-splitting results is not a result of this study.
record.test_reason: The study changes the SAE training objective (local MSE vs end-to-end KL, with or without downstream reconstruction losses). It reports a nearest-neighbour decoder cosine similarity, which the authors explicitly use as a proxy for feature splitting. This bears on V6's statement that other objectives change or reduce splitting. It does not measure splitting across dictionary sizes, input partitioning, or hierarchy.
record.authors_conclusion: Mostly correct. The authors propose e2e SAEs as a Pareto improvement: more performance explained with fewer total and fewer active features, at no interpretability cost but longer training. e2e+downstream keeps downstream reconstruction close to local SAEs. Local SAEs show tighter feature clustering, which the authors read as suggesting more feature splitting. They call the cosine metric a useful proxy that ignores semantic differences.
record.recipe_differences: The study compares standard local SAEs trained with activation reconstruction against end-to-end SAEs trained using output-distribution KL divergence, with an additional downstream reconstruction-loss variant.
record.method_sensitivity: The reported cosine-similarity differences depend on the SAE training objective; the summary does not give model-specific results for this metric.
record.problems: This summary reports cosine similarity only as a proxy for feature splitting and does not state which model the reported comparison uses. It does not directly measure whether split features partition the same inputs or test the claimed hierarchy.
record.rows_left_out: Performance explained, feature counts, reconstruction errors, interpretability, and training time are not rows because they do not measure the feature-splitting behavior at issue.

untested.parts: Whether splitting arises from correlated or hierarchical inputs. Whether SAE features say little about the model's own units. Matryoshka SAEs specifically. Any direct measure of splitting, such as parent/child features across dictionary sizes or input coverage, rather than within-dictionary cosine clustering.
Not tested. The dictionary-size scaling of splitting is only cited from Bricken et al.

missing.what: The authors state the cosine-similarity difference is not explained by SAE_local having more alive dictionary elements. This is a control relevant to the V6 proxy comparison.
missing.locator: Geometric analysis paragraph; Appendix A.7, Figure 7

missing.what: The Appendix A.7 comparison across all Pareto-frontier runs (dictionary sizes / sparsity levels) is referenced but its values are not given in this summary.

record.verdict_notes: Source is an Alignment Forum summary, not the full paper. The splitting evidence is a within-dictionary nearest-neighbour cosine proxy, which is weaker than a direct test of splitting. In comments, Logan Riggs notes the metric is asymmetric and can multiply-count clustered features. His Hungarian-matched replication (layer 6, first 10k features) reproduces the direction; it is commenter work, not the study's. The comments' cross-seed differences in e2e features do not concern splitting.

versions.untested_parts: No reported test of increasing dictionary size replacing a coarse feature with multiple finer features that partition its inputs and lie near its direction.
No reported test of the claimed splitting pattern across large models or open SAE releases.
No reported test of nested feature families, their input coverage, or whether they mirror a conceptual hierarchy.
No reported test of parent-child firing overlap or whether changing SAE size or sparsity fixes absorption.
No reported decomposition of larger-SAE latents into smaller-SAE latents or test for novel latents.

The study compares SAE objectives using a cosine-similarity proxy, but does not establish that splitting is an artifact on correlated or hierarchical inputs, that SAE features say little about the model's own units, or test Matryoshka SAEs.

rows.check: Subject and condition need fixing. The 0.04 figure is the Figure 3 comparison, apparently GPT2-small layer 6 SAEs matched for similar CE (per a commenter's replication note), not all Pareto-frontier runs. Appendix A.7 extends the comparison to all runs. The reduction is small next to the e2e result (0.04 vs 0.166), so it is partial.

source_check.correct: The 0.04 gap (bootstrapped 95% CI [0.037-0.043]) is the Figure 3 comparison. Its caption names the SAEs: GPT2-small layer 6 SAEs with similar CE loss increases (paper Table 1), so TinyStories-1M is not part of it. In Fig 3a the dashed lines (unlabelled in the caption) sit at about 0.54 for local and 0.50 for e2e+ds. The gap matches the stated 0.04 mean difference. The all-Pareto-runs measurement is a separate check (Appendix A.7, Figure 7). It is not in the post, which only says the difference is not explained by alive dictionary elements.

relation.reason: The study measures a proxy the authors name for feature splitting across training objectives on the same model and layer. That result bears on V6.

tranche.reason: The authors argue that MSE training spends capacity on less important features through feature splitting. Their results show the splitting proxy drops under e2e objectives. These are results that splitting depends on the objective and that V1 needs restating, which bears on V6.

source_check.notes: Figure 3 caption fixes both rows: GPT2-small layer 6 SAEs with similar CE loss increases (dashed-line gaps in 3a match 0.04/0.166). The all-runs check (Appendix A.7, Fig 7) is not in the post. No AI-directed instructions.

statements.correction: Figure 3 set, GPT2-small layer 6 SAEs with similar CE loss increase: SAE_local mean nearest-neighbour decoder cosine is 0.166 higher than SAE_e2e (95% CI 0.163-0.168). The authors call it a proxy for feature splitting. TinyStories-1M is not in this comparison.
statements.problem: 0.166 and the CI 0.163-0.168 are right, and they sit on GPT2-small, a model the statement names. But 'The model is not clearly stated' is wrong. 'GPT2-small/TinyStories dictionaries' is also too broad: the post's Figure 3 caption names GPT2-small layer 6 SAEs with similar CE loss increases, and TinyStories-1M is not in this comparison.

statements.correction: GPT2-small layer 6, similar-CE SAEs (Figure 3): SAE_local mean cosine is 0.04 higher than SAE_e2e+ds (95% CI 0.037-0.043) and 0.166 higher than SAE_e2e (95% CI 0.163-0.168). The all-runs check (Appendix A.7, Fig 7) is not in the post. The post says only that the gap is not explained by alive dictionary elements. Different pathways are shown by e2e's much worse downstream MSE (Figure 2), not tested against the cosine gap.
statements.problem: The values 0.04 (bootstrapped 95% CI 0.037-0.043) and 0.166 (95% CI 0.163-0.168) are in the text, but not on the condition the statement names. Both are the Figure 3 comparison on GPT2-small layer 6 similar-CE SAEs, not 'all Pareto-frontier runs', and the model is stated. The pathway explanation for the cosine gap is the catalog's inference. The authors infer different pathways from downstream reconstruction MSE (Figure 2), not from the cosine result.

statements.correction: Only a nearest-neighbour decoder cosine proxy, which the authors say ignores semantic differences. No check against model units.
statements.problem: Correct for this study. It has no direct splitting count and does not check split latents against the model's own units or computation. It gives only a within-SAE decoder-cosine proxy.

statements.correction: Same metric (within-SAE nearest-neighbour decoder cosine), GPT2-small layer 6 similar-CE SAEs. The local-minus-other gap is 0.166 for SAE_e2e (KL only) and 0.04 for SAE_e2e+ds (KL plus downstream MSE), so it varies with the training objective, not the metric.
statements.problem: The sentence is accurate: 0.166 vs SAE_e2e and 0.04 vs SAE_e2e+ds. But the gap comes from the compared SAE's training objective, using the same metric, so it does not show sensitivity to the factor named (metric choice).
